tagline: Piedmont farm country holds a brick mill and community barn quilts.
intro: The Mill Bridge Scenic Byway crosses the Mount Ulla area of western Rowan County, a landscape of rolling Piedmont hills, pastures and crop fields. NCDOT includes the route in its scenic-byway program, intended to introduce travelers to North Carolina’s history, geography and culture.

Farming here predates the registered community of Mill Bridge: farms and plantations occupied the area from the mid-1700s, while the community was registered in 1874. Kerr Mill began on Joseph Kerr’s plantation in 1823, later serving local tenant farmers after the Civil War. Commercial milling continued into the 1940s, and the restored mill became part of county-run Sloan Park.

On the western side of the area, Bear Poplar’s community barn quilt offers a separate excursion in Mount Ulla country. Mill Bridge brings together Kerr Mill and Thyatira Presbyterian Church. At Thyatira, off NC 150 west of Salisbury, the congregation remains active in a brick church completed in 1860.

moments.title: Mount Ulla
moments.text: Bear Poplar’s community barn quilt covers 500 square feet; the surrounding Mount Ulla area also has a Barn Quilt Trail. Adele Goodman of the Mount Ulla Historic Preservation Society began developing the Barn Quilt Trail in 2014–15. Residents installed the large mural on a store wall on July 8, 2019. Later that year, Elsie Bennett and Goodman published the personal stories behind its squares. It held the national size title until a mural in nearby Cleveland surpassed it in October 2021. Artists creating barn quilts in the area include Elsie Bennett, Pam Bostian and Susan Bostian.

moments.title: Kerr Mill
moments.text: Kerr Mill’s brick walls enclose a history of changing power. Joseph Kerr built it in 1823 on his Oakland plantation, where he enslaved thirty to forty people. After the Civil War, the mill served local tenant farmers on a small scale. An undershot waterwheel, fed by a millrace and canal, later gave way to a steam-powered roller mill in 1887 and a diesel engine in 1925. Commercial operation ended in the 1940s. James Sloan and his wife offered it to Rowan County’s citizens in 1973; the restored building is part of Sloan Park.
moments.notice: The two-story brick mill rests on a stone foundation beneath a gable roof.

moments.title: Mill Bridge
moments.text: Every postmaster at Mill Bridge was a woman during the post office’s life from 1874 to 1903. Mary E. McCubbin took the first appointment when it opened on July 23, 1874. The agricultural community centered on Thyatira Presbyterian Church in the 1880s. The site has held four successive houses of worship, beginning with a log building above and west of the cemetery’s older section. Worship at the site reaches back to at least 1750, but the present Gothic Revival building dates from 1858–1860. The congregation remains active, beside a cemetery with gravestones from the mid-1750s.
